grh_e70784eebb69a5dec473.title: Voodoo Lady
paragraphs: Blind neighborhood spiritual healer Miss Rabbit uses powders, bones, prayer and powers she has learned to treat with caution after earlier arrogance cost her sight. A desperate mother asks her to save a nine-month-old son whose unexplained condition is steadily killing him, and Miss Rabbit agrees even after being warned that such an intervention may demand a terrible price. The child suddenly recovers, leaving the doctors unable to explain the change. When grateful neighbors return to thank Miss Rabbit, they find her mysteriously gone, leaving the cost of the miracle unanswered.

[[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes David Downing, Hans Conried, Helen Martin, June Foray, and Kim Hamilton. Other credited names include Elliott Lewis as director, Elliott Lewis as producer, Odie Hawkins as writer, and [[person|vincent-price|Vincent Price]] as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_e723f37644959113165a.title: Melody Ranch - I Hate to Say Goodbye 47-06-29
paragraphs: Gene opens with 'I Hate to Say Goodbye to the Prairie' and later recalls a ranch-versus-ranch rodeo competition decided by the saddle-bronc event. His draw, a paint horse later known as Skyball Paint, seems almost tame in the chute and then explodes into a violent bucking ride that throws Gene and costs his ranch the contest. Gene later acquires the horse and stages repeated attempts by skilled riders to stay aboard; after others, including the boastful Blackie, are quickly thrown, Gene finally rides the paint for eleven seconds, wins the prize money and earns the horse himself.

The cast includes The King Sisters, Johnny Bond, The Cass County Boys, Gene Autry, and Carl Cotner and His Orchestra. Other credited names include William Burch as director and Lou Crosby as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9fa945fb6505daf2|Spearmint Gum]].

grh_e721009504cc67533d41.title: Younger Generation
paragraphs: Linda Munson learns that Lieutenant Alan Gibbons, the young man she had planned to marry before her mother objected that they were too young, has returned from war badly wounded and discouraged. She insists that she is old enough to decide where she belongs and goes to the military hospital with Dr. Christian. Alan is ashamed of his scarred face and has lost the will to continue treatment, but Lindas unwavering love convinces him that his future is not over. Their courage persuades the older generation, including Lindas mother, that the young people deserve more faith than they have been given.
